title: They Lost Four Straight Finals in Two Years. In Singapore, Satwik and Chirag Finally Won — and Made History.
excerpt: The Indian pair became the first to win the Singapore Open doubles title, ending a two-year drought by beating the world No. 1 and No. 3 pairs back to back. Now they lead India's charge at the Indonesia Open.
body:
They had not won a BWF World Tour title in nearly two years. They had reached four finals since the 2024 Thailand Open and lost every one of them. On Sunday in Singapore, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty finally ended the drought — and made history while doing it.

The Indian pair defeated Indonesia's Fajar Alfian and Muhammad Shohibul Fikri 18-21, 21-17, 21-16 in the Singapore Open 2026 final, becoming the first Indian men's doubles combination to win the title. It was their ninth career BWF World Tour trophy and their third Super 750 crown, following back-to-back French Open titles in 2022 and 2024.

The Road Through Singapore

SatChi's run to the title was not a gentle draw. In the semifinals, they dismantled the world No. 1 pair — South Korea's Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae — in straight games, 21-19, 21-18. The Koreans had entered the tournament riding a 34-match unbeaten streak, the longest in men's doubles this century. That streak ended in 52 minutes.

The final against Alfian and Fikri, the world No. 3, was a different kind of test. The Indonesian pair took the first game 21-18 in a tight battle where neither side held a meaningful lead until the closing stages. At that point, lesser pairs might have folded. Satwik and Chirag had been in this position before — four times in two years — and lost.

Not this time. Satwik's explosive smashes and Chirag's commanding net play reasserted themselves in the second game. The Indian pair built an 11-8 cushion at the interval and held firm despite a late Indonesian push, winning 21-17. In the decider, they raced to an 11-5 lead. Alfian and Fikri clawed back to 12-11, but a devastating sequence of Satwik smashes extended the lead to 20-15. Alfian's return found the net on championship point.

Why This Matters for the Diaspora

Badminton doubles has historically been dominated by East Asian pairs — Indonesia, South Korea, Japan, and China have monopolised the sport's biggest titles for decades. India's singles players, from Prakash Padukone to PV Sindhu, have broken barriers. But in doubles, the glass ceiling remained.

Satwik and Chirag have been chipping away at it since their 2022 Commonwealth Games gold. They became the first Indian pair to reach the world's top three in rankings, the first to win a Super 750 title, and now the first to conquer Singapore. For Indian-origin badminton enthusiasts watching from Houston, London, or Melbourne, the pair's rise represents a structural shift, not just an isolated result.

Indonesia Open: The Next Challenge

There is no rest. The Indonesia Open, a BWF Super 1000 event — one tier above the Singapore Open — began in Jakarta on June 2. Satwik and Chirag are the fourth seeds and will face Malaysia's Khai Xing Kang and Aaron Tai in the first round, a pair they defeated in the Singapore quarterfinals.

India's full contingent in Jakarta is substantial. PV Sindhu leads the women's singles entry, with a potential second-round clash against world No. 1 An Se-young of South Korea. Lakshya Sen, Kidambi Srikanth, H.S. Prannoy, and Ayush Shetty compete in men's singles. Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand return to the women's doubles circuit after three months out with injuries.

The tournament runs through June 7, with live coverage available on JioStar in India.

What's Next

The Indonesia Open result will shape Olympic qualification rankings heading into the second half of 2026. For Satwik and Chirag, who carry the expectations of a billion people every time they step on a doubles court, the Singapore Open title was not just a win — it was proof that the drought was a delay, not a decline.

Sources: BWF, Badminton World Federation rankings, RevSportz, The Bridge
